title: Objectwise Brown Hom representability for locally small categories
statement: Fix a universe $w$. Let $C,D$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category], with arbitrary object and Hom universes, such that every Hom set is equivalent to a type in universe $w$. Suppose both categories have coproducts indexed by types in universe $w$, and $C$ is compactly generated relative to those coproducts [def-pc-compactly-generated]. Let $F:C\to D$ be exact and preserve every such coproduct. For any fixed $Y\in D$, the functor $X\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_D(F(X),Y)$ on $C^{op}$ is representable: there is $G_Y\in C$ and bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_C(X,G_Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(F(X),Y)$ natural in $X$.

proof.text: Use ShrinkHoms.equivalence to replace both categories by equivalent categories with Hom types in universe w. Transfer the additive, zero, shift and distinguished-triangle structures. Equivalences preserve coproducts. The natural additive Hom bijections identify the direct-sum-to-Hom maps for each transported generator with the original maps, so compactness is preserved. Their coproduct stays a weak generator because shifts, zero objects and nonzero maps are preserved and reflected. Thus the transported source is compactly generated in universe w.

Transport F by the inverse source equivalence and target equivalence. This functor is exact and preserves w-indexed coproducts. Apply lem-pc-brown-representability-right-adjoint with its indexing universe and both Hom universes equal to w. The resulting adjunction represents Hom from the transported F into the image of the fixed Y.

Pull the representing object and its natural Hom bijections back along the equivalences. Composition with the fully faithful equivalences gives the required bijections for the original categories, natural in X.
